body:
First step of the simulation-thread / immutable-Scene renderer revamp: the simulation must be able to run on a thread other than the one that loaded it. Today the synchronized RNG is a `thread_local` default engine, so a game advanced on another thread silently diverges (the prototype hit exactly this).

## Changes
- **`Game::syncRandom`** — each game owns its synchronized stream, saved/restored with the game. `syncStep`, `executeOrder`, load and save bind it via the existing `SyncRandScope`; `setGameHeader` seeds it directly. `Game::bindRandom()` for other code that advances a game.
- **Session guard** — while an engine session runs, a synchronized draw without a bound stream is counted (`unboundSyncRandDraws()`); `GLOB2_SYNC_RAND_STRICT=1` aborts on it.
- `setSyncRandSeed` / `get|setSyncRandState` act on the bound stream, else the thread default (map generation and tools unchanged).
- Menu colony game owns its stream instead of swapping it into the global engine.
- **Presentation RNG** — particles use `GameGUI::effectsRandom` instead of C `rand()`; rule documented: visual effects never use `syncRand()`.
- **`test/check_sim_thread.py`** — runs new games (two maps, 8 AI types), a generated map, a v121 save and save continuation with a baseline and a candidate executable; requires identical checksum sidecars, final saves and replay bytes (bytes that vary between two baseline runs are excluded and reported — see below).
- Tests that build games directly now bind the game's stream (`BoundGameRandom`), and RNG-continuity checks inspect the game's stream (they would otherwise pass vacuously against the untouched global stream).
- `test/fixtures/guard-area/off-path-checksums.txt` regenerated: its old values depended on RNG draws leaked from earlier games in the same test case. Verified on master: skipping those earlier scenarios reproduces exactly the new tick-0 map checksum.

## Verification (macOS, Apple clang 21, M3)
- `GLOB2_SYNC_RAND_STRICT=1 python3 test/check_sim_thread.py <this build> --baseline <master 75ad507e7 build>` → new-game, new-game-maxima, generated-load, legacy-v121, resume: all identical; zero unbound draws.
- `python3 test/run_tests.py --no-display --exclude-tag map-generators` → 336 passed, 0 failed; display cases `HighResolution*`, `TorusRender/*` → 5 passed; `MenuColonyHarness check` and `navigation` pass. Map-generator suite running locally with a longer timeout (CI job covers it).
- Not verified locally: Linux/Windows (CI), Android/iOS, browser. No simulation behavior change is intended; cross-platform checksum equality is unchanged by construction but covered by CI's existing determinism jobs.

## Compatibility / feel
No save, replay or network format change; saves still store and restore the same RNG words. No gameplay or visual change except particle randomness now coming from a different (presentation-only) generator.

## Pre-existing issue found (not fixed here)
Two runs of the same binary on `balanced.map` produce replays differing in the replay header's map `SHA1` (apparently unset for maps loaded without one) and a 4-byte field in saved AI state (near the Cabino player's data). Neither affects checksums or final saves.

title: Give each game its own synchronized random stream
